metadata.note: The Rock Island's own main line from Kansas into Texas -- Topeka, Herington, Wichita and Caldwell across Kansas, then down the Chisholm Trail through Enid, El Reno, Chickasha, Duncan and Waurika, and into Fort Worth. It was built by two Rock Island subsidiaries: the Chicago, Kansas and Nebraska laid the Kansas half in 1887 and crossed the Indian Territory from 1889, and the Chicago, Rock Island and Texas -- separately incorporated because Texas required it -- brought the tracks into Fort Worth on Aug 1 1893. Its best-known train was the Twin Star Rocket of 1945, Minneapolis to Houston, whose discontinuance in March 1967 ended Rock Island passenger service between Kansas and Texas. The line is still there and busy with Union Pacific freight, but freight-only years are not drawn (CLAUDE.md Rule 1).
sources: https://www.kansashistory.gov/p/chicago-rock-island-and-pacific-railway-records/13753 (Kansas Historical Society) -- SEEN ONLY AS A SEARCH-ENGINE QUOTE, the page itself was not read: a contract of Mar 19 1887 between the Union Pacific and the Chicago, Kansas and Nebraska for joint use of UP track between Kansas City and North Topeka for 999 years.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: NOT DRAWN, Kansas City to Topeka: the Twin Star Rocket and the Rock Island's other Texas trains ran from Kansas City to Topeka over the UNION PACIFIC, not over their own iron -- a contract of Mar 19 1887 gave the Chicago, Kansas and Nebraska joint use of UP track between Kansas City and North Topeka for 999 years, and the Rock Island's own line began at Topeka. That is why this layer starts at Topeka rather than Kansas City. The trackage-rights fact was read only as a search-engine quotation of the Kansas Historical Society page, not from the page itself, so treat it as unconfirmed. OpenStreetMap has no continuous ex-Rock Island alignment between Kansas City and Topeka either, which is consistent with there never having been one. NOT DRAWN, Fort Worth to Houston: the Twin Star Rocket continued south over the Burlington-Rock Island, the jointly owned line already drawn in data/burlington_rock_island.geojson. NOT DRAWN, the Twin Star Rocket north of Topeka: its Minneapolis-St Paul-Des Moines-Kansas City half is a separate corridor that has not been traced, so the train appears here only as the operator of this line, not as a feature of its own. Every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh is an estimate; no Rock Island public timetable or Official Guide page was consulted. The year the Texas Rocket entered service is not sourced. No documented mileage was found for Topeka-Fort Worth or for any of its legs, so the traced lengths are unvalidated against a source; the tag-composition figures in each feature's geometry_quality are the evidence that the alignment is the right railroad's. Intermediate stations were not compiled beyond the corridor waypoints, so the route is drawn as a line rather than station by station.
geometry_sources: Traced on real track in OpenStreetMap by corridor-constrained Dijkstra over every railway=rail/abandoned/disused/razed way in the corridor, then simplified Douglas-Peucker at 40 m. The graph was restricted to ways tagged old_railway_operator=CRI&P plus untagged track, with every way carrying another railroad's operator tag excluded, so the route cannot wander onto a competitor's parallel grade.

Overpass API (maps.mail.ru mirror), bbox dumps of every railway way in the Kansas City-Caldwell, Caldwell-Waurika and Waurika-Fort Worth corridors, pulled 2026-08-27. Endpoints and corridor waypoints are OSM place nodes.

Per-leg result: Kansas (Topeka-Caldwell) 333.6 km, 95% CRI&P-tagged, 3.7 km bridged; Oklahoma (Caldwell-Waurika) 331.2 km, 100% CRI&P-tagged, 0 km bridged; Texas (Waurika-Fort Worth) 181.5 km, 100% CRI&P-tagged, 0.62 km bridged.

properties.line: Chicago, Kansas and Nebraska: Topeka – Caldwell
properties.speed_source: estimated: an 1880s Kansas prairie line; unsourced
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced, 207.1 mi Topeka–Herington–Wichita–Caldwell on the surviving alignment, today the Union Pacific's Topeka and Lost Springs Subdivisions and the Enid Subdivision. 95% of the traced length runs on ways OpenStreetMap tags old_railway_operator=CRI&P, which is the check that the trace stayed on Rock Island rails rather than a parallel Santa Fe or Missouri Pacific line. 3.7 km of the 333.6 km is straight-line bridging between OSM fragments, in ten pieces, the largest 1.63 km. No documented mileage was found to check the total against. Straight-line repair 2026-08-29: 2 ruled segments totalling 36 mi replaced with OpenStreetMap-traced rail geometry (see geometry_repairs for the OSM lines each one followed).

segments.note: The Chicago, Kansas and Nebraska -- a Rock Island creature from the start, financed with about twenty-five million dollars advanced by the Rock Island in exchange for nearly all its stock -- laid the Topeka-Herington-Caldwell line in 1887. The first train reached Wellington on Nov 10 1887 and the first train pulled into Caldwell that December, at the edge of the Indian Territory, where the railhead stopped until Congress allowed a crossing. Drawn to 1889, when the Rock Island took the company over outright; the later years are the Rock Island features (CLAUDE.md Rule 4). Frequency estimated, unsourced
sources: Segment-level: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago,_Kansas_and_Nebraska_Railway (construction record, 1887: "Horton KS - Topeka KS - Herington KS - Caldwell KS"; the CK&N was formed in 1885 with Rock Island money and nearly all its stock held by the Rock Island; "In 1889, the CK&N was failing to make payments on its interest, so the Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific Railroad took over"); https://www.co.sumner.ks.us/about_sumner_county/county_history/railroad_history/index.php (Sumner County, Kansas railroad history) (the first train, a mixed passenger and freight train, reached Wellington Nov 10 1887, and in December the first train pulled into Caldwell). Headway and speed are estimates.

properties.line: Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific: Topeka – El Reno
properties.speed_source: estimated: a new prairie main line; unsourced
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced, 316.2 mi. Same trace as the Topeka–Fort Worth feature, cut at the OSM place node for El Reno (1.28 km from it). See that feature for the tag-composition check. Straight-line repair 2026-08-29: 6 ruled segments totalling 98 mi replaced with OpenStreetMap-traced rail geometry (see geometry_repairs for the OSM lines each one followed).

segments.note: The Rock Island took the Chicago, Kansas and Nebraska over in 1889 and pushed the railhead across the Indian Territory the same year, Caldwell to El Reno, following the Chisholm Trail. El Reno to Minco came in 1890 and the Red River was reached by 1892. Drawn to El Reno for these years because that is the 1889 railhead; the 1890-92 extensions ran ahead of it toward Texas and are not drawn separately. Frequency estimated, unsourced
sources: Segment-level: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago,_Kansas_and_Nebraska_Railway (construction record, 1889: "Caldwell KS - El Reno IT"; 1890: "El Reno IT - Minco IT"; the company "entered Oklahoma Territory in 1888, building tracks south along the Chisholm Trail and reaching the Red River by 1892"). Headway and speed are estimates, and no timetable was consulted for what actually ran to El Reno in these years.

properties.line: Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific: Topeka – Fort Worth
properties.speed_source: estimated: a secondary main line, fast running on the prairie; unsourced
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced, 525.5 mi in three legs that share endpoints exactly: Topeka–Caldwell 207.1 mi, Caldwell–Waurika 205.7 mi, Waurika–Fort Worth 112.7 mi. Tag composition, the check that the trace stayed on Rock Island rails: the Oklahoma leg is 100% ways tagged old_railway_operator=CRI&P (UP Enid and Duncan Subdivisions, no bridging at all), the Texas leg 100% (UP Duncan Subdivision, one 0.62 km bridge), the Kansas leg 95% (UP Topeka and Lost Springs Subdivisions and the Enid Subdivision, 3.7 km of bridging in ten pieces, largest 1.63 km). Endpoints snapped 0.91 km from the OSM place node for Topeka and 0.72 km for Fort Worth. No documented mileage for Topeka-Fort Worth was found, so the total is unvalidated against a source. Straight-line repair 2026-08-29: 6 ruled segments totalling 98 mi replaced with OpenStreetMap-traced rail geometry (see geometry_repairs for the OSM lines each one followed).

segments.note: The Chicago, Rock Island and Texas Railway -- chartered Jul 15 1892, a separate company because Texas law required railroads operating in the state to be incorporated in it -- built south from the Oklahoma line, and the tracks out of Bridgeport ran southeast into Fort Worth on Aug 1 1893. That completed a Rock Island route from Kansas into Texas. Frequency estimated, unsourced
sources: Segment-level: https://www.tshaonline.org/handbook/entries/chicago-rock-island-and-texas-railway (Texas State Historical Association) (the Chicago, Rock Island and Texas Railway was chartered Jul 15 1892 to build from the north boundary of Montague County south to Weatherford; by 1893 fifty-five miles had been built from the Oklahoma-Texas state line to Paradise; the charter was amended in 1893 to allow a branch to Fort Worth and Dallas, and "The tracks out of Bridgeport went southeast to Fort Worth, reaching there on August 1, 1893"). Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: The Chicago, Rock Island and Gulf Railway was chartered May 13 1902 to carry the line on from Fort Worth toward Galveston, and the Rock Island's Texas trains ran through. By the 1930s a Kansas City-Dallas streamliner, the Texas Rocket, was working this route. Frequency estimated, unsourced
sources: Segment-level (corporate): https://www.tshaonline.org/handbook/entries/chicago-rock-island-and-gulf-railway (Texas State Historical Association) (the Chicago, Rock Island and Gulf Railway was chartered May 13 1902 in the interest of the Rock Island to extend the system from Fort Worth to Galveston). Texas Rocket: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twin_Star_Rocket (in 1945 "one train set from the Kansas City-Dallas Texas Rocket was transferred to the new Twin Star Rocket"). NOT SOURCED: the year the Texas Rocket entered service, the 1902 and 1945 segment boundaries as service events, and the headway.

segments.note: The Twin Star Rocket entered service Jan 14 1945 -- the only new streamliner the government allowed into service during the war -- running the 1,363 miles from Minneapolis to Houston as trains 507 and 508, the longest north-south run under one railroad measured by great circle distance. It came down this line through Topeka, Herington, Wichita, Caldwell, Enid, El Reno, Chickasha, Duncan and Waurika into Fort Worth. Frequency estimated, unsourced
sources: Segment-level: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twin_Star_Rocket (introduced Jan 14 1945; the only new streamlined train permitted to enter service in World War II; northern terminal the Milwaukee Road's Minneapolis depot, southern terminal Houston 1,363 miles away; trains 507 and 508; the article's route map lists Topeka, Herington, Wichita, Caldwell, Enid, El Reno, Chickasha, Duncan, Waurika, Fort Worth, Dallas among the stops). Headway is an estimate; the daily frequency is sourced but the 1440-minute figure is a modelling choice.

segments.note: In October 1964 the Twin Star Rocket was cut back from Houston to Fort Worth, leaving passengers to change to the Sam Houston Zephyr -- itself cancelled in 1966. The Twin Star Rocket was discontinued in March 1967, and with it the Rock Island's through passenger service from Kansas into Texas. Frequency estimated, unsourced
sources: Segment-level: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twin_Star_Rocket ("In October 1964, the terminus was curtailed from Houston to Fort Worth, requiring passengers to transfer to the Sam Houston Zephyr. That train was cancelled in 1966. In March 1967, the Twin Star Rocket was discontinued."). NOT SOURCED: whether any other passenger train outlasted the Twin Star on this line -- 1967 is used as the end of passenger service on the strength of the Twin Star alone.
